newsitem.title: USA: Texas Muni Power A-plus on negative outlook - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Texas Muni Power A-plus on negative outlook - Fitch.

text.p: Following a recent review by Fitch Investors Service, Texas Municipal Power Agency's (TMPA) $1.1 billion of outstanding revenue bonds remain at "A+" with a negative outlook.
A decision whether to affirm or lower their rating is expected in the next six months.
A Fitch Competitive Indicator (FCI) score of 2.78 was assigned to TMPA, which is in line with the industry average, but below other 'A+' rated utilities.

Over the last few years, TMPA has significantly lowered its operating costs, while converting the Gibbons Creek power plant to burn western coal. In addition, the agency is in the process of completing the final upgrades to the plant, which should increase kilowatt hour (kwh) output and result in stable wholesale rates.

While TMPA has made many improvements over the last year and a half, it remains unclear if the plant will be able to operate at projected levels. Fitch believes a more accurate assessment of the agency can be made after the system has operated over the next several months.
TMPA is a joint action agency providing wholesale power to four member systems' serving approximately 130,000 customers.
The agency's rating is supported by generally competitive retail rates at the member level, a diverse customer base and historically good financial performance.

Other credit strengths include savings acquired from the fuel conversion of the power plant and a downsizing of the staff to 150 employees from 345. These savings have resulted in a 20% reduction in wholesale rates to about 4 cents per kwh.
There are concerns that as the electric industry becomes more competitive TMPA will not have the flexibility it needs to lower wholesale rates.

Other credit risks include the agency's heavy asset concentration in a single generating unit, the need for a more detailed stranded cost recovery plan and uncertainties as to how TMPA fits into the member systems' future energy supply plans.
Since the Gibbons Creek plant changed over to western coal from lignite on March 31, 1996, it has operated in the 415 to 430 megawatt (mw) range, compared with its previous capacity of 405 mw.

However, additional modifications are needed to reach the plants projected capacity level of 452 mw. Other enhancements include a turbine overhaul and upgrade, which will be installed in the next few months. This should increase plant capacity to 462 mw and further improve the units efficiency levels. The extra kwh output is an important part of the agency's strategy to hold down rates.

TMPA has also converted its power sales contracts (PSCs) with its members from all-requirement contracts to take-or-pay agreements. Under the new PSCs, each member will be responsible for their fixed allocated portion of the agency's costs.

The new contracts provide the members' with the flexibility to acquire additional power from sources other than the agency, while firming up their contractual commitment to TMPA. SOURCE Fitch Investors Service
